demo.title: Demo
demo.intro: Watch a short video walkthrough of the app. It comes in English, Russian and Hebrew.
demo.note: The videos are streamed from demos.gimlai.app when you open this page. Nothing from your plan is sent.

swiftness.title: swiftness.co.il tutorials
swiftness.intro: Step-by-step video tutorials for swiftness.co.il, the Pension Clearing House site where you order the consolidated pension report. The videos are in Hebrew only.
swiftness.note: These two videos are embedded from YouTube (privacy-enhanced mode) when you open this page, so YouTube may receive your IP address. Nothing from your plan is sent.

welcome.title: Your retirement plan, on your device
welcome.subtitle: Estimate your retirement income, and when you could retire, from your Israeli pension, savings and investments.
welcome.loadSavedHint: Used the app before? Choose the .json file you saved earlier with “Export data” in Settings.

about.title: What this app does
about.body: You enter your pension, provident and study funds, stocks, Bituach Leumi pension and expected spending. The app turns them into a retirement picture.

points.income: Your monthly income after tax, year by year
points.earliest: The earliest age you could retire
points.rules: Israeli tax and Bituach Leumi rules are built in
points.scenarios: What-if scenarios and a market-risk check

about.saveBody: Your plan lives in this browser. Use “Export data” in Settings to save it as a file, and “Import data” there (or “Load my saved data file” above) to load it again, later or on another device. Keep an exported file as a backup: clearing browser data erases the plan.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.lead: Your financial data never leaves this device.

points.local: No account and no server. Everything is saved in this browser only.
points.files: Nothing is uploaded. Files you import are read on this device only.
points.lookups: A few optional public lookups are made: the dollar rate (only a currency pair and a date), Israeli inflation figures and public stock-price files. None carries amounts or personal details, and the first two can be switched off in Settings.

flow.title: Get started
flow.intro: Go through the My Data steps in order, or jump to any of them. Only your age and desired retirement age are required. Everything is saved on this device and you can change it at any time.
flow.fastTrackBadge: Fast track fills most of this

steps.personal: Your age, gender, salary and family details.
steps.pensionSavings: Pension, provident and study funds, with balances, deposits and fees.
steps.equity: Stocks, employee share plans (ESPP, ESOP), bank deposits and other investments.
steps.expenses: What you expect to spend in retirement.
steps.assumptions: Returns, inflation and other settings. Sensible defaults are used if you skip this.

result.title: See your results
result.body: The Dashboard shows your earliest feasible retirement age and income after tax. Projections lets you compare scenarios.

fastTrack.title: Fastest start: import your Pension Clearing House report
fastTrack.intro: The report lists all your pension, provident and study funds in one file. Importing it fills in most of steps 1 and 2 for you. You check every value before anything is added.

personal.salary: Monthly gross salary, taken from your deposits
personal.marital: Marital status, offered as a suggestion for you to confirm

pension.accounts: Every account: provider, product type, balance and severance balance
pension.deposits: Deposit rates for you and your employer
pension.fees: Management fees and the investment track
pension.annuity: Estimated monthly pension and conversion factor

fastTrack.stillYours: your desired retirement age, expenses, stock holdings, bank deposits, other assets and assumptions.
fastTrack.howOrder: Order the report at swiftness.co.il (the Pension Clearing House service). You verify your identity and pay a small fee.
fastTrack.howImport: It arrives by email, usually within about one business day, as a password-protected file. Choose that file here.
fastTrack.howReview: Review the suggested values and apply the ones you want. The file is read on this device only.
fastTrack.sampleHint: Want to see how it works first? The import page has a sample report to try.

dashboard.title: Dashboard

feasibility.title: Earliest Feasible Retirement
feasibility.feasibleNow: Your current assets already cover your target retirement spending.
feasibility.bothRetire: Both of you retire together: you at {{age}}, your spouse at {{spouseAge}}.
feasibility.averageMarkets: In average markets, where your assumed return is earned every year.
feasibility.confidentSame: The same age holds with {{percent}}% confidence.
feasibility.confidentNone: With {{percent}}% confidence: not reachable by age {{age}}.
feasibility.confidentPending: Checking the earliest age with {{percent}}% confidence…
feasibility.notFeasible: Your target retirement spending isn't reachable by age {{age}} with your current savings and contributions. Try lowering expenses, saving more, or adjusting your assumptions.
feasibility.noTarget: Enter your expected monthly retirement expenses to see how soon you could retire.

bituachLeumi.title: Bituach Leumi Old-Age Pension
bituachLeumi.ownAges: Each pension starts at its owner's own age.
bituachLeumi.spouseSupplement: Includes a {{amount}} per month supplement for a spouse without a pension, from age {{start}}.
bituachLeumi.spouseSupplementUntil: Includes a {{amount}} per month supplement for a spouse without a pension, from age {{start}} until age {{end}}, when the spouse's own pension starts.
bituachLeumi.deferral: Includes a {{percent}}% supplement for deferring past the statutory age ({{age}}).
bituachLeumi.usingOverride: Based on the amount you entered from Bituach Leumi.
bituachLeumi.excluded: The state pension is not included in your projections.
bituachLeumi.notEligible: Based on your insured years you may not qualify yet: the pension requires {{lifetime}} insured months, or {{recent}} within the last 10 years.
bituachLeumi.incomeSupplementHint: With total income below {{amount}} you may be entitled to an income supplement (means-tested; not included in this estimate).

sourceAccess.title: Access to your savings
sourceAccess.annuities: Accounts paying a monthly annuity: {{amount}} (included in your income)
sourceAccess.bridgeLimited: Until age {{age}} only part of your savings is accessible, which limits your sustainable income. If all your savings were available it would be {{income}} per month.
sourceAccess.rulesAsOf: Access rules as of {{date}}. Early-withdrawal penalties are not modeled.

tax.title: Income tax in retirement
tax.lowestYear: These figures are for the year with the lowest income after tax (age {{age}}); other years are higher.
tax.noTax: No income tax is expected on this income.
tax.perSpouse: Each spouse is taxed on their own income.
tax.includedBrackets: Pension and annuity income at the {{year}} income tax brackets, less your credit points.
tax.includedExemption: From the statutory retirement age, {{percent}}% of a pension of up to {{ceiling}} per month is exempt (the qualifying annuity exemption).
tax.includedExemptionRising: From the statutory retirement age, {{percent}}% of a pension of up to {{ceiling}} per month is exempt in {{year}} (the qualifying annuity exemption). By law the share rises to {{finalPercent}}% from {{finalYear}}, and the plan uses the share of each year.
tax.includedHealthTax: Before the statutory retirement age a pension bears health tax: {{reducedRate}}% up to {{bracket}} per month and {{fullRate}}% above it.
tax.includedCapitalGains: Withdrawals from an investment provident fund and other investments are taxed at {{rate}}% on the real gain only.
tax.includedExempt: State pensions and study fund withdrawals are tax-free.
tax.includedSection102: Employer shares under Section 102 (capital gains route, held through the 24-month trustee period): the grant-date value is taxed at your marginal rate and the growth above it at {{rate}}%. A sale within the 24 months, or the ordinary-income track, is taxed entirely at your marginal rate.
tax.includedSection102Contributions: The ordinary-income part of employer shares also bears health tax ({{healthReducedRate}}% up to {{bracket}} per month, {{healthFullRate}}% above it) and, before the statutory retirement age, Bituach Leumi contributions ({{niReducedRate}}% / {{niFullRate}}%), on income up to {{ceiling}} per month.
tax.notIncludedSection102: Not included for employer shares: the higher rate for a holder of 10% or more of the company, option strike prices, and ESPP discounts.
tax.notIncluded: Not included: Bituach Leumi contributions of people who retire before the statutory age, health tax on income other than a pension or employer shares, other credit points (for example for children), and tax planning between spouses.

kpi.incomeSustained: The most your savings can pay each month so that they last to age {{age}}.
kpi.incomePlanFunded: At your planned {{amount}} a month your usable savings last through age {{age}}.
kpi.incomePlanShortfall: At your planned {{amount}} a month your usable savings run out at age {{age}}.
kpi.incomeBasis: The lowest year of retirement, at your age {{age}}. After tax, in today's money.
kpi.surplusNote: to spare each month after your planned spending
kpi.shortfallNote: short of your planned spending each month
kpi.surplusScale: {{percent}}% above your planned spending of {{planned}} a month
kpi.shortfallScale: {{percent}}% below your planned spending of {{planned}} a month
kpi.surplusAverageOnly: In average markets only: {{percent}}% of simulated market histories fund your spending.
kpi.noSpendingNote: Enter your planned spending to see this.
kpi.successNoteAll: All {{paths}} simulated market histories fund your spending. That is not certainty about real outcomes.
kpi.successNoteShare: Share of {{paths}} simulated market histories that fund your spending.
kpi.successQualifier: Based on your inputs and model assumptions; not a guarantee.
kpi.successAssumptions: Assumes {{returnPct}}% return, {{inflationPct}}% inflation and {{volatilityPct}}% volatility a year.
kpi.householdTimingNote: Counted until the later of the two.
kpi.netWorthNote: Everything you have entered, at today's values.
kpi.netWorthDebts: This is what you own: loans and a mortgage are not subtracted. Enter their monthly payments as a retirement expense; the plan counts them every month of retirement.

dashboard.moreDetail: More detail: irregular costs, earliest feasible age, access to your savings, Bituach Leumi and income tax

snapshot.title: What you will live on
snapshot.subtitle: Monthly amounts are in today's money; income is before tax.
snapshot.withdrawalRateNote: Your planned spending as a share of the funds available in the first year, before tax. Rates above about 4% rely more on investment returns.
snapshot.withdrawalRateUnavailable: Needs planned spending and funds available at retirement

income.title: Where the monthly income comes from
income.intro: Before tax, in today's money. A payment keeps arriving for life; a withdrawal comes out of your savings, which the plan runs down by age {{endAge}}.
income.stagePayments: Once your lifelong payments have all started, age {{age}}
income.noStateBenefits: Bituach Leumi is not in your projection.
income.continues: Lifelong payments do not stop at age {{age}}: {{amount}} a month of them (state benefits and pension annuities) keeps arriving after it, while the savings are used up by then.
income.timelineLink: See every year in the retirement timeline
income.none: No retirement income is estimated yet. Add your pension and savings in My Data.

retireChecks.title: Could you retire at…?
retireChecks.subtitle: Whether your plan covers your planned spending if you retire at that age. A spouse retires at the same time.

dashboard.statusOnTrack: You're on track to meet your retirement goal.
dashboard.statusOnTrackAverage: On track in average markets only.
dashboard.statusAverageDetail: Your plan funds your spending if markets return what you assumed every year, but only {{percent}}% of simulated market histories do.
dashboard.statusConfidentSpending: With {{percent}}% confidence you could spend about {{amount}} a month, against your goal of {{target}}.
dashboard.statusChecking: Checking your plan against simulated markets…
dashboard.statusShortfall: You may need additional savings to meet your retirement goal.
dashboard.statusShortfallLevers: Your plan falls short of your planned spending. Any one of these would close the gap, in average markets:

levers.spendNote: instead of the {{planned}} you plan, with the same retirement age and savings.
levers.retireNote: instead of {{planned}}, with the same spending and savings.
levers.saveNote: until you retire, at the return you assumed.

dashboard.householdChartNote: The projection covers your whole household. The age axis shows your age.

coverNotice.title: Insurance cover that ends when deposits stop
coverNotice.intro: Death cover inside active pension accounts lapses a few months after the deposits stop. Nothing in your numbers changes until you choose what to do.

item.self: Your cover ends at about age {{endAge}}, {{years}} years before the age it is needed until ({{needAge}}).
item.spouse: Your spouse's cover ends at about age {{endAge}}, {{years}} years before the age it is needed until ({{needAge}}).

gaps.title: Improve your estimate
gaps.intro: Optional details that would change your result. Your estimate already works without them.

items.retirementAge: No retirement age entered, so every figure assumes {{age}}.
items.spouseRetirementAge: No retirement age entered for your spouse, so every figure assumes {{age}} for them.
items.retirementSpending: No expected retirement spending: the funding gap, plan status and earliest retirement age can't be worked out.
items.noSavings: No savings entered yet, so the projection starts from zero.
items.spouseMissing: You are marked as married but your spouse's age is empty, so the plan covers only you.
items.accountType: Accounts without a product type: {{count}}. They are treated as a fully accessible pension fund; set the type to apply access rules.
items.accountStatus: Accounts without a status: {{count}}. They are assumed to receive no further deposits.
items.annuityInputs: Pension accounts without a conversion factor or monthly pension estimate: {{count}}. They are treated as savings spent by age {{horizon}}, not as a lifelong pension. Add the factor from your annual statement.
items.salary: No monthly gross salary: deposits to your actively contributing accounts ({{count}}) are not projected.
items.spouseSalary: No monthly gross salary for your spouse: deposits to their actively contributing accounts ({{count}}) are not projected.
items.contributionRates: Actively contributing accounts with no contribution rates: {{count}}. No further deposits are projected for them.
items.gender: Gender is not set, so the defaults for a man apply (state pension age 67, 2.25 tax credit points).
items.spouseGender: Your spouse's gender is not set, so the defaults for a man apply (state pension age 67, 2.25 tax credit points).
items.holdingGain: ESPP or private shareholdings with no purchase price and no declared gain: {{count}}. Their gain is left untaxed, so your income after tax may be overstated. Enter the purchase price.

dashboard.emptyBody: Complete your profile to see your personalized retirement projection.

portfolio.title: What you have
portfolio.intro: The rows add up to the Net Worth Today figure above. Select a row to see or change what you entered.

groups.lockedNote: can be spent only from the age shown

portfolio.dollarShare: {{amount}} ({{percent}} of the total) is priced in US dollars, so its value in shekels moves with the exchange rate.
portfolio.returnNote: Every asset above is assumed to grow at the same {{returnPct}} a year (before inflation), whether it is a deposit, a share or a pension fund.
portfolio.unvested: Not counted above: {{amount}} of employer shares that have not vested yet. The projections add the part that will have vested by retirement.

fx.boi: Share prices are converted at {{rate}} ₪ per US dollar (Bank of Israel rate on {{date}}).
fx.typed: Share prices are converted at {{rate}} ₪ per US dollar, the rate you typed.
fx.fallback: Share prices are converted at {{rate}} ₪ per US dollar, a built-in rate, because none was entered or looked up.

portfolio.employerShare: Employer shares are {{percent}} of this total, all in one company.
portfolio.employerShareLink: See what a fall in their price would do
portfolio.concentration: {{name}} shares are {{percent}} of this total, all in one company.
portfolio.concentrationUnnamed: One of your share holdings is {{percent}} of this total, all in one company.
portfolio.concentrationLink: See what a fall in share markets would do

budget.title: Retirement budget
budget.intro: Your estimated net income in retirement is {{income}} per month. Here is how it compares with the essential minimum and with your full planned budget.
budget.caveat: Both budgets are compared with the same estimated net income. The risk analysis tests the full planned budget, so being above the essential line does not make the essentials certain.
budget.typedTotal: Your plan uses one typed monthly figure, so it cannot tell essential spending from discretionary spending. Itemise your expenses to see the essential minimum against your income.

irregular.title: Irregular costs included in your monthly average
irregular.intro: These are paid once a year or less often. The plan spreads each one evenly over the months between payments, so it shows up as a steady monthly cost. This is an average, not a payment schedule: the plan does not know when any of them falls due.
irregular.reserve: The largest single payment is {{amount}} ({{name}}). When it falls due you need that much in funds you can reach; the monthly average does not show it.
irregular.snapshotNote: Includes {{amount}} per month of irregular costs, averaged.

legend.required: Needed to build your plan. You can't continue without it.
legend.recommended: Not blocking, but your result changes. A default is assumed when it is empty.
legend.reference: Saved and exported with your data, but not used in any calculation yet.

importance.legendOptional: Fields with no tag are optional refinements; a sensible default applies when they are empty.

person.householdTotal: Household total counted in your plan:

equityCategoryTitle.personalBrokeragePurchase: Privately purchased stocks at a glance

fxRateSource.boi: Bank of Israel rate of {{date}}. Type another rate to use your own.
fxRateSource.typed: The rate you entered. Shekel values use it until you switch back to the automatic rate.
fxRateSource.fallback: A rough built-in rate, as no exchange rate has been looked up. Type your own, or allow lookups in Settings.

validation.summary: Some required details need fixing before you can continue. The first one is highlighted.
validation.retirementAfterAge: Retirement age must be greater than your current age.
validation.spouseRetirementBeforeAge: Your spouse's retirement age can't be lower than their current age.

personal.label: Personal
personal.householdNoteUnmarried: Joint (household) calculations with a partner are available only for married couples. Common-law partners count as married. Choose "Married" to add your partner.
personal.householdNoteMarried: Joint calculations are available only for married couples. Open the Partner tab to add your partner's details.
personal.monthlyGrossSalaryHelper: Used to project ongoing pension and savings deposits until retirement. Leave empty to assume no further deposits.
personal.creditPointsHelper: Leave empty to use the default: 2.25 for a man, 2.75 for a woman. Used to work out the income tax on your retirement income.
personal.bituachLeumiIntro: Estimates your state old-age pension from your gender, age and insured years. It is paid from the statutory retirement age, even if you stop working earlier.
personal.bituachLeumiInclude: Include the state pension in projections
personal.bituachLeumiInsuredYearsHelper: Leave empty to assume you have been insured since age 21.
personal.bituachLeumiOverride: Monthly pension from Bituach Leumi's calculator
personal.bituachLeumiOverrideHelper: Optional. Replaces the estimate; enter the amount in today's money.
personal.spouseIntro: Enter your partner's age to plan together. Their pension accounts and Bituach Leumi pension then join your projections, and you stop contributing and claim at your own ages. Only married couples can share calculations; common-law partners count as married.
personal.spouseAgeHelper: Leave empty to plan on your own.
personal.spouseRetirementAgeHelper: Household spending starts when the later of you two retires. Enter their current age if they have already stopped working.
personal.spouseMonthlyGrossSalaryHelper: Used to project their pension and savings deposits until they retire. Leave empty to assume no further deposits.
personal.spouseCreditPointsHelper: Leave empty to use the default for their gender: 2.25 for a man, 2.75 for a woman.
personal.spouseBituachLeumiIntro: Estimated from their gender, age and insured years. If your spouse has no pension of their own, you may also receive a spouse supplement.
personal.spouseBituachLeumiInclude: Include their state pension in projections
personal.spouseBituachLeumiInsuredYearsHelper: Leave empty to assume they have been insured since age 21. Enter 0 if they have never been insured.
personal.spouseBituachLeumiOverride: Spouse's monthly pension from Bituach Leumi's calculator

pensionSavings.label: Pension & Savings
pensionSavings.noAccounts: No accounts added yet. Add your pension funds, provident funds, managers insurance policies, or study funds.
pensionSavings.noAccountsSpouse: No accounts added for your partner yet. Add their accounts here, or import their Clearing House report.
pensionSavings.partnerNotCountedMarried: These accounts are not counted yet. Enter your partner's age on the Personal tab to include them in your joint plan.
pensionSavings.partnerNotCountedUnmarried: These accounts are not counted. Joint calculations are available only for married couples: set your marital status to Married on the Personal tab to include them.
pensionSavings.removeConfirmBody: This permanently removes the account and its details from your profile.
pensionSavings.otherAssetsHelp: The plan counts this with your other investments: money you can spend at any time, growing at the plan's return. Leave out a home you live in and any property you do not plan to sell.
pensionSavings.otherAssetsShared: Counted once for the whole household, not per person.

fields.policyNumberHelper: As printed on your annual statement. For your own reference and cross-checking; not used in calculations.
fields.fundIdHelper: The fund's identifier on your statement, for cross-referencing it with published fund data; not used in calculations.
fields.lifeAnnuityFrom60: Take as a life annuity from age 60
fields.lifeAnnuityFrom60Helper: Optional. At 60 the balance can move to a paying fund and be taken as a monthly annuity, which is tax-free, instead of a lump sum taxed at 25% on the real gain. Once moved, it can only be taken as an annuity. While this is ticked, the plan does not spend the balance as capital. The rule comes from secondary sources and is not confirmed.
fields.lifeAnnuityFrom60NeedsInput: Nothing changes yet: enter a conversion factor or an estimated monthly annuity under Annuity parameters. Until then this fund stays in the plan as a lump sum.
fields.contributionsHelper: Percent of your monthly gross salary deposited each month. Only counted while the account status is "Active — contributing". Typical pension: 6% employee, 6.5% employer, 6% severance.
fields.contributionsHelperOwner: Percent of the account owner's monthly gross salary deposited each month. Only counted while the account status is "Active — contributing". Typical pension: 6% employee, 6.5% employer, 6% severance.
fields.monthlySalaryBase: Monthly gross salary these rates apply to
fields.monthlySalaryBaseHelper: Leave empty to use the monthly gross salary from the Personal step. Fill it when accounts are funded from different salaries, for example two employers or a study fund that covers both.
fields.annuityParametersHelper: Used for pension funds, managers insurance and an investment provident fund taken as an annuity. Enter the monthly annuity from your statement (today's money), or enter the conversion factor (typically 140–215) to compute it from the balance. A pension fund uses the factor as entered; managers insurance uses it only when you tick the guaranteed factor; for an investment provident fund enter the factor of the fund that will pay the annuity. The annuity starts at age 60, or right away if the account is already paying an annuity.
fields.monthlyRiskDeductionHelper: Paid out of each deposit for the insurance cover. The projection counts it as the cost of cover, not as savings, so it is taken off the amount added to the balance.
fields.monthlySurvivorsSpousePension: Monthly survivors' pension to a spouse
fields.survivorSpousePercent: Spouse's survivors' pension, % of pensionable salary

equity.label: Investments & Deposits
equity.noEsop: No ESOP/RSU grants added yet. Add one if your employer grants you shares or options.
equity.noEspp: No ESPP purchases added yet. Add one if you buy shares through an employee stock purchase plan.
equity.noPrivateTrade: No private trades added yet. Add shares you bought yourself, outside an employer plan.
equity.removeConfirmBody: This permanently removes the holding and its details from your profile.

vesting.title: Vesting schedule (optional)
vesting.intro: Enter the whole award as the quantity above, then say how it vests: equal batches on a regular schedule, counted from the grant date. It starts with the usual RSU schedule: 20 quarterly batches of 5%, the first three months after the grant. Change it to match your award, or clear the fields if everything has already vested. The 24-month holding period counts from the grant date. Batches that vest after you retire are lost, unless the box below says the grant keeps vesting.
vesting.introBulk: Applies to every row below: equal batches on a regular schedule, counted from each row's date. It starts with the usual RSU schedule: 20 quarterly batches of 5%, the first three months after the grant. Change it to match your awards, or clear the fields if everything has already vested.
vesting.needs: Enter the grant date and the quantity above, and valid numbers here, to see the schedule.
vesting.summary: Shares vested so far: {{vested}}. Not yet vested: {{unvested}}.

splits.asReported: Quantities and prices are as originally reported (before later stock splits)
splits.asReportedHelper: Keep this on for numbers taken from a broker or clearing-house statement: they are restated in today's shares using the stock's split history. Turn it off if you already converted them.
splits.singleNote: A split since this date means each share became ×{{factor}}: it will be saved as {{quantity}} shares. A price you typed is divided by the same factor; an estimated price is already adjusted.

bulk.symbolHelper: All rows below are for this stock. To add another stock, use this dialog again.
bulk.csvHelperPersonal: Paste CSV or tab-separated text with the columns Date, Symbol, Quantity and, optionally, Share price. A first line with column names is understood too.
bulk.csvHelperEmployer: Paste CSV or tab-separated text with the columns Date, Quantity and, optionally, Share price. A first line with column names is understood too.
bulk.ignored_one: 1 line could not be read and was ignored.
bulk.ignored_other: {{count}} lines could not be read and were ignored.
bulk.splitsNote: Rows marked with × were restated in today's shares, after the stock split since their date.
bulk.priceNote: A missing or zero price is filled in with the closing price on that date when the stock is in the downloaded data. You can change it later by editing the holding.
bulk.needsSymbol: Enter the stock symbol to add these rows.

fields.currentMarketPriceHelper: Today's price per share, in USD. It gives the holding its value.
fields.entryPriceGenericHelper: Per share, in USD: the price on the purchase or grant date. Choose a category to see exactly which price it expects.
fields.tickerHelper: Start typing to pick a stock from the S&P 500 list. Other tickers work too; enter their prices by hand.
fields.priceHintEntry: The purchase or grant price was filled in from the closing price on {{date}}, the last trading day on or before the date you entered.
fields.priceHintCurrent: The current price was filled in from the closing price on {{date}}, the latest in the downloaded data.
fields.priceHintAdjusted: Prices come from a public S&P 500 dataset and are adjusted for later stock splits and dividends. Enter the quantity as you hold it today, and expect older prices to be a little lower than the price quoted at the time. Check them against your broker statement, and edit any value to use your own.
fields.entryRateHelper: Shekels per US dollar on the purchase or grant date. Filled in automatically; type your own to replace it.
fields.rateHint: The dollar rate was filled in from the Bank of Israel rate of {{date}}, the last business day on or before the date you entered. It is saved with the entry for your records; the tax calculations do not use it. For ESPP and private shares, list each purchase under the details below to have its rate used.
fields.esppPriceOnPurchaseDateHelper: Per share, in USD: the market price on the purchase day, before the ESPP discount. The taxable gain is measured from it. What you actually paid goes under the details below.
fields.personalPurchasePriceHelper: Per share, in USD: what you paid on the purchase date. Used for tax: the gain above it is taxed when you sell, unless you declare the gain under More details.
fields.sectionEmployerGrantDetails: Tax and vesting - affects your estimate
fields.employerGrantIntro: Used to tax these shares at sale: under Section 102 (capital gains route) the grant-date value is taxed at your marginal rate and the growth above it at the capital gains rate.
fields.keepsVestingAfterLeaving: This grant keeps vesting after I leave
fields.keepsVestingAfterLeavingHelper: Leave this off if every unvested share is lost when you leave. Turn it on only if your plan lets unvested shares keep vesting after you leave, for example on retirement.
fields.costBasisAtGrantHelper: Per share, in USD: the fair market value on the grant date for Israeli tax. Some plans define it as the average price over the 30 trading days before the grant, so check your plan documents. Leave empty if unknown: then the whole value is taxed as a capital gain.
fields.sectionPersonalPurchaseDetails: More details: personal brokerage (gain, tax rate)

bankDeposits.title: Bank deposits
bankDeposits.noDeposits: No bank deposits added yet. Add a fixed-term or variable-rate shekel deposit, with or without a CPI link.
bankDeposits.removeConfirmBody: This permanently removes the deposit and its details from your profile.

fields.cpiLinked: Linked to the Consumer Price Index (CPI)
fields.autoRenew: Renews automatically at maturity (keeps earning interest)

bankDeposits.rateHelper: The deposit's own rate is used to value it today. From today it is treated like your other investments and grows at the plan's return, not at this rate.
bankDeposits.cpiLinkedHelper: Deposits always shown in shekels (NIS). When linked, the principal and/or rate track the CPI in addition to the interest rate above.
bankDeposits.maturityHelper: Used only to stop interest at this date when the deposit does not renew. The plan does not time your withdrawals by it: bank deposits are counted with your other investments as money you can use at any time, growing at the plan's return.

expenses.label: Expenses
expenses.retirementMonthlyHelper: Without this the plan shows your retirement income but can't tell whether it is enough.
expenses.modeLabel: How do you want to enter your spending?
expenses.modeHintTotals: Type one monthly figure for what you expect to spend in retirement.
expenses.modeHintDetailed: Build the figure from a list of expenses, in today's money like the rest of the plan. A bill that comes every few months, or a big purchase every few years, is spread into a monthly amount.
expenses.plannedHelper: The plan compares your retirement income with this full amount.
expenses.typedTotalKept: The total you typed ({{amount}}) is kept and comes back if you switch to one total.
expenses.itemisedKept: Your itemised list ({{amount}}) is kept and comes back if you switch back to it. The plan uses the total above.
expenses.plannedEmpty: Nothing is planned until you add expenses, so the plan has no retirement spending to measure against.

coverCosts.line: {{option}}, {{amount}} per month, from age {{from}} to age {{to}}
coverCosts.note: Paid out of your own pocket on top of the spending above, and taken out of your income and savings in the projections. You cannot edit it here: change it under "Cover after I stop working" in Personal.

expenses.noItems: No expenses yet. Choose from the suggested list or add your own. Enter what you expect to pay in retirement.

form.title: Expense
form.name: Name
form.amountHelper: What one payment is expected to cost in retirement, in today's money.

expenses.removeConfirmBody: It will no longer count towards your retirement spending.

suggestions.title: Choose from suggestions
suggestions.intro: Tick the expenses that apply to you and, if you like, enter what one payment will cost in retirement. How often each is paid is a typical guess; you can change anything afterwards, and fill in amounts later.

catalog.vehicleLicence: Annual vehicle test and licence fee
catalog.medicalProcedures: Medical procedures and tests not covered by insurance

assumptions.label: Assumptions
assumptions.presetRealReturn: Real return about {{value}} per year (after inflation)
assumptions.basisNote: Return and inflation are yearly, nominal rates. The plan takes inflation off, so results are shown in today's money.
assumptions.volatilityNote: Market volatility is set separately (now {{value}} per year) and stays the same for every preset.
assumptions.horizonNote: How long the plan assumes you live. A later age spreads your savings over more years, so the monthly income they can sustain is lower. Bituach Leumi and pension annuities are paid for life and carry on after it. For a couple, the plan runs until the younger of you reaches this age. The Projections page shows what each age changes.
assumptions.volatilityHelp: How much yearly returns typically swing up or down. Used only by the risk analysis. A diversified portfolio is often 8% to 18%.

cpi.title: Israeli inflation (Central Bureau of Statistics)
cpi.subtitle: For reference. Your plan uses the value above.
cpi.statusUnavailable: Could not reach the Bureau of Statistics. Showing built-in figures up to {{month}}.
cpi.statusOff: Online lookup is turned off in Settings. Showing built-in figures up to {{month}}.

assumedRetirementAge.label: Assumed retirement age
assumedRetirementAge.self: Using an assumed retirement age of {{age}}, because you haven't entered yours.
assumedRetirementAge.spouse: Using an assumed retirement age of {{age}} for your spouse, because you haven't entered theirs.

assumptionsSummary.label: Assumptions in use
assumptionsSummary.values: Investment return {{returnPct}} (before inflation), the same for every asset, inflation {{inflation}}, market volatility {{volatility}}. All per year.

projections.scenarioScope: Applies to the charts and cards on this page, except the earliest feasible age and the retirement age comparison, which do not follow this choice.
projections.scenarioEarlyFloor: In these scenarios Early never goes below age {{age}}, so for your plan it matches Standard and is switched off. The age comparison can go lower.

projections.netIncomeNote: Each bar is one year's sustainable income before tax, split into what you keep and the income tax paid.
projections.householdNote: The plan covers your whole household and ages are yours. Early and delayed scenarios move both retirement dates.

risk.title: Risk analysis
risk.intro: Markets don't return the same amount every year. This replays your plan on {{paths}} random market histories to see how often your desired spending lasts.
risk.noTarget: Enter your expected monthly retirement expenses (in My Data) to test them against market ups and downs.
risk.calculating: Simulating possible markets. The rest of the page is ready to use.
risk.noYears: There are no retirement years to test before age {{age}}.
risk.successLabel: Chance your desired spending lasts to age {{age}}

band.strong: High confidence: most market histories fund your spending.
band.fair: Moderate confidence: some market histories run short.
band.weak: Low confidence: many market histories run short.

risk.confidentLabel: Monthly spending that holds up in {{percent}}% of histories
risk.confidentHint: After tax, in today's money. Your goal is {{target}} a month.
risk.shortfallAge: In the histories that fall short, the spending usually goes unfunded from about age {{age}}.
risk.howRandom: Each year's market return is random, with a typical swing of {{volatility}}% (your market volatility assumption). Nothing else varies.
risk.howMedian: The typical (median) line is built on your projection's return, so it stays close to the projection above.
risk.howFixed: Bituach Leumi, annuity payments and other fixed income do not vary. Every investment earns the same return in a given year, which is cautious.
risk.howTax: Your desired spending is after tax, so it is converted to {{gross}} a month before tax using your plan's tax rate ({{percent}}%). Tax is not recalculated for each history.
risk.howSeed: The same random histories are used every time, so the same inputs always give the same result.
risk.notForecast: A model, not a forecast. Real markets can do worse than any of these histories.
risk.qualifier: Based on your inputs and model assumptions; not a guarantee.
risk.allPaths: All {{paths}} simulated histories fund your spending. That is not certainty about real outcomes.
risk.assumptions: Assumes {{returnPct}}% return, {{inflationPct}}% inflation and {{volatilityPct}}% volatility a year.

history.title: Historical backtest
history.intro: How would your plan have gone in the real past? This replays it on what US stocks and bonds actually returned, starting in each year from {{first}}.
history.noTarget: Enter your expected monthly retirement expenses (in My Data) to test them against the real past.
history.noYears: There are no retirement years to test before age {{age}}.
history.basisAsHappenedHint: The real history, good years and bad. It averaged {{history}}% a year.
history.basisMatchedHint: The same ups and downs, shifted to average your plan's {{plan}}% a year.
history.successLabel: Starting years that fund your spending to age {{age}}

band.all: Your spending held up in every starting year.
band.strong: Your spending held up in nearly all starting years.
band.fair: Your spending held up in most starting years, but some ran short.

history.survivableLabel: Monthly spending that every starting year could fund
history.survivableHint: After tax, in today's money. Your goal is {{target}} a month.
history.worstShort: Hardest start: {{start}}, replaying {{range}}. Spending first goes unfunded at age {{age}}.
history.worstOk: Hardest start: {{start}}, replaying {{range}}. It still left {{amount}} at age {{age}}.
history.returnsLine: Your plan assumes {{plan}}% a year after inflation. This portfolio averaged {{history}}% over {{range}}.
history.whyHigher: Why the two risk tests can disagree: this test replays a portfolio of {{stocks}}% stocks that averaged {{replayed}}% a year, above the {{plan}}% your plan assumes. The simulation earns your {{plan}}% on average, so it starts from a lower return, and adds {{volatility}}% yearly volatility.
history.whyLower: Why the two risk tests can disagree: this test replays a portfolio of {{stocks}}% stocks that averaged {{replayed}}% a year, below the {{plan}}% your plan assumes. The simulation earns your {{plan}}% on average, so it starts from a higher return, and adds {{volatility}}% yearly volatility.
history.whySimilar: Why the two risk tests can disagree: both start from about the same average return ({{plan}}% in your plan, {{replayed}}% here), so they differ only in how returns vary. This test replays real history in order; the simulation draws random years with {{volatility}}% yearly volatility.
history.chartTitle: Net worth from each starting year
history.howWindows: For each starting year, your plan's first year gets that year's real return, the second year gets the next, and so on to age {{age}}. Only starts with a full run of history count: {{count}} of them, from {{first}} to {{last}}.
history.howMix: Returns are for {{stocks}}% US stocks (S&P 500 with dividends) and {{bonds}}% 10-year US government bonds, rebalanced every year, after US inflation and before fees and tax.
history.howOverlap: Neighbouring starting years share most of their history, so they are not independent tests. Read the result as what happened in the past, not as a probability.
history.howCurrency: This is US history in US purchasing power. The shekel, Israeli inflation and Israeli markets are not modelled.
history.howTax: As in the risk analysis, your desired spending is after tax, so it is converted to {{gross}} a month before tax using your plan's tax rate ({{percent}}%).
history.notForecast: The past is only one history. The future can be worse.
history.mixHint: A hypothetical model portfolio. It is not based on your own holdings.

compare.title: Compare retirement ages
compare.intro: Pick any three ages at which you could retire to see how your income and savings change. Per month, in today's money.
compare.independent: This comparison has its own ages. It does not follow the retirement scenario chosen above.
compare.coupleNote: Your spouse's retirement moves by the same number of years as yours.
compare.noTarget: Enter your expected monthly retirement expenses (in My Data) to see how each age compares to your goal.
compare.footnote: Income after tax is the lowest year of retirement, as on the Dashboard. Savings are shown at the age the household starts drawing.

ladder.title: When your money becomes usable
ladder.intro: What you can spend when you retire and what opens up later, in today's money. Savings are shown at their value when you retire.
ladder.lateVesting: Company shares worth about {{amount}} at today's price vest after you retire (the first batch on {{date}}), and your grant keeps vesting after you leave. The plan counts them as usable from retirement, so it may be too optimistic in the first years.
ladder.howValues: Savings are shown at their value when you retire. A pot that is still locked keeps growing until it opens.
ladder.howRules: Pension funds, managers insurance and provident funds open at age {{age}}. A study fund opens when its liquidity date passes, by default {{years}} years after you joined. Investment provident funds and other savings, including bank deposits, are treated as usable at any time.
ladder.howPayments: Annuities and Bituach Leumi are monthly payments, not savings, so they are not added to the usable total.
ladder.howReadOnly: This only shows your plan. It changes none of its numbers, and early-withdrawal penalties are not modeled.

sourceCost.title: What each source costs to draw on
sourceCost.intro: The extra tax when you raise your spending by {{step}} a month, in today's money, and take it from one source. Compare them to see which sources are cheapest to draw on.
sourceCost.managementFee: Management fee {{percent}} a year of the balance

giveUp.studyFund: Tax-free growth. Money you take out stops growing free of tax.
giveUp.investments: Flexibility. This money is treated as usable at any time, and only its real gain is taxed, at a flat rate.
giveUp.investmentProvidentFund: Flexibility. Only the growth since today is taxed, at a flat rate, and this money is usable at any time.
giveUp.section102Shares: Employer shares. The grant-date value is taxed as salary at your brackets, with health tax and Bituach Leumi before the statutory retirement age; only the growth above it is taxed at a flat rate.
giveUp.ordinaryIncomeShares: All of it is taxed as salary at your brackets, with health tax and Bituach Leumi before the statutory retirement age.
giveUp.pension: Taxed as a pension. From the statutory retirement age part of it is exempt; before then it bears health tax.

sourceCost.howMarginal: Each figure is the extra tax if you raise your net spending by {{step}} a month and take all of it from that source, in the first year that source can be used, on top of what your plan already draws.
sourceCost.howSame: Every source is assumed to earn the same return, so the table compares tax only, not how much each source would have grown.
sourceCost.howGroups: Money of the same kind is combined and weighted by its value when you retire. Annuities and Bituach Leumi are payments, not savings, so they are not listed.
sourceCost.howFee: The management fee is shown only if you entered one, and it is not part of the tax.
sourceCost.howReadOnly: This only shows your plan. It changes none of its numbers. It is an estimate, not tax advice.

unvested.title: Leaving before your shares vest
unvested.intro: Company shares that have not vested by your retirement date are lost, unless the grant keeps vesting after you leave. Amounts use today's share price and are before tax.
unvested.lost: If you retire on {{date}}, you lose {{shares}} of unvested company stock (about {{value}}).
unvested.next: Staying {{period}} longer, until {{date}}, would keep another {{shares}} (about {{value}}).
unvested.nextGain: That adds about {{amount}} a month to your net retirement income.
unvested.howRule: A batch of shares vests on its date. Batches that vest after your retirement date are lost, unless the grant is marked as one that keeps vesting after you leave.
unvested.howGain: The monthly gain compares your net retirement income with the same plan if the next batch had already vested. It uses today's share price and the plan's tax rules.
unvested.howReadOnly: This only shows your plan. It changes none of its numbers.

cover.title: Cover that ends when deposits stop
cover.intro: The death cover inside your active pension accounts lapses a few months after the deposits stop. Here are the ways to handle the years until the cover is no longer needed: what each leaves uncovered and what it costs. The app shows the numbers; it does not say which choice is better.
cover.upperBound: At most: some accounts lack a conversion factor
cover.costUnknown: Not known: enter it in My Data
cover.costNote: Costs are paid out of your own pocket and shown in today's money. Choosing an option saves it in My Data and adds its cost to your spending in the projections, so your income and savings change. You can add the cost and other details there.
cover.editInMyData: Edit the details in My Data
cover.howWindow: The cover continues at no cost for about 5 months after the last deposit. An insurance arrangement can extend it by up to 24 months at your cost. After that it ends, unless you buy a term policy or the fund lets you keep paying. These rules are in the constants file and are still to be verified.
cover.howGapMoney: The survivors' pension is the amount your accounts state for the spouse. Without the insurance, your balance alone would pay about the balance divided by the account's conversion factor each month. The gap is the difference. It is a rough, low-confidence estimate, and it leaves out orphans' pensions and lump sums.
cover.howCost: The pension insurance costs what you enter, or else the risk premiums now deducted from your accounts. A term policy costs what the insurer quotes, which you must enter. The total is the monthly cost over the years it is paid.
cover.howScope: Only death cover for survivors is compared. Disability cover is not included.

stress.title: If things go wrong
stress.intro: Your plan run again with one thing going wrong. Amounts are in today's money.
stress.exposureDollar: {{amount}} of your savings are held in dollars: the shares you would still have when you start drawing, at today's prices and exchange rate.
stress.rowDollar: The dollar falls {{percent}} against the shekel
stress.rowBoth: Both: employer shares fall {{shares}} and the dollar falls {{dollar}}
stress.short: Short of your desired spending by {{amount}} a month
stress.howEmployer: Employer shares are the company's grants and the shares bought through its employee plan (ESPP). Shares you bought yourself are not counted, even in the same company.
stress.howMarket: A share-market fall lowers the price of every share you hold, the ones you bought yourself too, but not the dollar. Pension and provident fund tracks are not broken down into stocks and bonds, so they are not part of this test.
stress.howDollar: A weaker dollar lowers what your dollar holdings are worth in shekels, and the gain that is taxed. Savings in shekels stay as they are.
stress.howIncome: Each income is the sustainable monthly income after tax when the whole plan is run again, the same figure as on the Dashboard.
stress.howRetirement: Only the savings you hold when you start drawing count. Unvested shares that you would lose are left out.
stress.howReadOnly: This only shows your plan. It changes none of its numbers. It is a what-if, not a forecast.

longevity.title: If you live longer
longevity.intro: Your plan run again to a later age. The same savings are spread over more years, so each extra year of life lowers the monthly income they can sustain. Amounts are in today's money.
longevity.change: {{amount}} a month compared with your plan
longevity.lasts: Your usable savings cover it to age {{age}}
longevity.runsOut: Your usable savings run out at age {{age}}
longevity.short: Net income is short of it by {{amount}} a month
longevity.howIncome: Each income is the sustainable monthly income after tax when the whole plan is run again to that age, the same figure as on the Dashboard for your plan's age.
longevity.howLifelong: Bituach Leumi and pension annuities are paid for life, so they do not shrink with a longer life. Only the savings are spread over more years.
longevity.howSpending: The right-hand column spends your desired monthly spending from retirement and shows when your usable savings would run out, if they do before that age.
longevity.howReadOnly: This only shows your plan. It changes none of its numbers. It is a what-if, not a forecast.

withdrawal.title: Which savings to draw on first
withdrawal.intro: Your spending is the same whichever savings pay for it, but the tax is not. Compare the orders and choose the one the whole plan should use.

proRata.name: Evenly
proRata.description: Every unlocked source pays the same share of each year's spending.

taxableFirst.name: Taxable money first
taxableFirst.description: Other investments and shares first, then the investment provident fund, then pension money. The tax-free study fund is last.

lowestTaxFirst.name: Lowest tax first
lowestTaxFirst.description: The tax-free study fund first, then money taxed only on its gain, then pension money. Money taxed as ordinary income is last.

withdrawal.firstShortfall: First year below your desired spending
withdrawal.peakTaxable: Highest taxable income in a year
withdrawal.surtaxYears: Years above the surtax threshold ({{threshold}} a year)
withdrawal.deltaNote: The grey figures show the change compared with the order in use.
withdrawal.identical: For your savings every order gives the same tax each year, so the choice makes no difference to this plan.
withdrawal.tradeoff: No order wins on every line: the one with the lowest total tax can leave you with less in your leanest year. Look at all of the lines before you choose.
withdrawal.usedEverywhere: The order you choose is used for the whole plan: the Dashboard, the income chart and the timeline.
withdrawal.howSameGross: Every order draws the same amount from the same savings, and all of your savings earn the same return, so what is left at each age is the same. Only the tax, and so the income you keep, changes.
withdrawal.howLocked: Money that is still locked is not drawn on until it opens. The order applies to all of your unlocked savings together; each spouse is taxed on their own part.
withdrawal.howRisk: The risk analysis and the historical test do not depend on the order.
withdrawal.howEstimate: Tax is estimated with today's rules. This is not tax advice, and no order is a recommendation.

timeline.title: Retirement timeline
timeline.intro: Which sources pay for each stage of retirement, in today's money.
timeline.plannedBasis: Your planned spending of {{amount}} a month, year by year, before tax: payments and withdrawals as they would happen, until your usable savings run out. The part nobody pays is shown as unfunded.
timeline.nothingPays: Nothing pays: the usable savings are used up and no recurring payment remains.

cashFlow.title: Cash flow by year
cashFlow.intro: Year by year at your planned spending of {{amount}} a month: what comes in, what is withdrawn from which savings, the tax, and the part nobody pays. All amounts are monthly averages for the year, in today's money, before tax unless stated.
cashFlow.taxNote: Tax is an estimate on what you receive and withdraw. As in the Net Worth Projection, it is shown but not added to the spending that has to be funded.
cashFlow.irregularNote: Large irregular costs, about {{amount}} a month, are spread evenly inside the spending, because the plan has no due years for them.
cashFlow.coverNote: Survivors' cover premiums are paid on top of the spending, so in those years the bars can rise above the dashed line.

projections.bankDepositsNote: Your bank deposits are counted in “Investments (deposits, shares, cash)”: the plan treats them as money you can use at any time, growing at the plan's return. Each deposit's own maturity date, early-withdrawal terms and renewal are not modeled individually.
projections.netIncomePlannedNote: The dashed line is your planned spending after tax.

basis.netWorthNoSpending: No retirement spending is entered, so nothing is drawn after you retire: this line shows your savings growing, not running out. Add your expected expenses in My Data to see how long they last.
basis.netWorth: Your savings if you spend {{amount}} a month from retirement, your planned spending, in today's money.
basis.netWorthFunded: Your usable savings cover it through age {{age}}.
basis.netWorthShortfall: From age {{age}} your usable savings no longer cover it, and the unfunded part is not shown on this line.
basis.income: The most your savings and pensions are estimated to pay each month, before tax, so that they last to age {{age}}. This is not your planned spending and does not change when you change it.
basis.continues: Lifelong payments (state benefits and pension annuities) still pay {{amount}} a month at age {{age}}, before tax, and keep paying after it; the savings are used up by then.
basis.incomeShortfall: At your planned {{amount}} a month your usable savings run out at age {{age}} (see Net Worth Projection), so payments from savings would not continue at this level after that age.

split.note: Recurring payments keep arriving without using up your savings: Bituach Leumi and any pension annuity that has started. Withdrawals are money taken out of your savings to cover the rest, so they can include your original capital, not only returns. The plan does not separate interest or dividends from capital.
split.noteShort: Withdrawals come out of your savings and can include your original capital, not only returns.
split.investmentsPool: {{source}} form one pool: bank deposits, private shares, vested employer shares, cash and other assets are drawn on together and cannot be split here.

path.title: What shapes this path
path.retire: Age {{age}}: you retire and start drawing on your savings.
path.retireNoSpending: Age {{age}}: you retire. No spending is entered, so nothing is drawn from your savings.
path.retireHousehold: Age {{age}}: the later of you two has retired, and the household starts drawing on its savings.
path.retireHouseholdNoSpending: Age {{age}}: the later of you two has retired. No spending is entered, so nothing is drawn from your savings.
path.shortfall: Age {{age}}: at your planned spending your usable savings run out.
path.unvestedRange: Why the line starts above your total today: {{amount}} of employer shares have not vested yet. They vest between ages {{from}} and {{to}}, but the plan counts them from the start of the line, at today's share price.
path.unvestedOne: Why the line starts above your total today: {{amount}} of employer shares have not vested yet. They vest at age {{from}}, but the plan counts them from the start of the line, at today's share price.
path.annuity: Age {{age}}: {{kind}}. The {{capital}} of capital becomes an annuity of {{monthly}} a month. It is paid out as monthly income, so it is no longer a balance you can spend and it leaves the line.
path.tableNote: Balances are at the end of each year, in today's money. Capital that has become an annuity is no longer a balance: it is paid out as monthly income. Capital that is still locked until its access age is included.
path.poolNote: Bank deposits, shares and other holdings are modeled as one investments pool, shown in the {{pool}} column. The model has no separate path for each of them.

riskBasis.title: What the risk tests rest on
riskBasis.intro: The risk analysis and the historical backtest below test simple models. They do not replay your bank deposits, shares and pension investments one by one.
riskBasis.risk: All your savings earn the plan's {{returnPct}} a year before inflation, with a typical market swing of {{volatility}} a year. This is one rate for everything, not the return of each of your own holdings.
riskBasis.backtest: A hypothetical portfolio of US stocks and bonds, starting at {{stocks}} stocks and {{bonds}} bonds. You change the mix in the test itself. It is a model, not a reconstruction of what you own.
riskBasis.exposureNote: Neither test treats them differently from your shekel savings.
riskBasis.exposureLink: See what a fall would do

section.titleSpouse: Spouse's cover after they stop working
section.introSelf: Pension funds and managers insurance include death cover for your family (a survivors' pension or a lump sum). It runs on for a few months after your deposits stop and then lapses. Choose how you want to handle the years from then until your pension opens. The app shows the gap and the cost; it does not say which choice is better.
section.introSpouse: Your spouse's pension funds and managers insurance include death cover for the family. It runs on for a few months after their deposits stop and then lapses. Choose how to handle the years from then until their pension opens. The app shows the gap and the cost; it does not say which choice is better.
section.option: What to do about the cover
section.optionHelper: Nothing changes in your plan until you choose.
section.needUntilAgeHelper: Leave empty to use the earliest pension age ({{age}}). Enter a later age if your family will still depend on the cover.
section.monthlyCostKeepHelper: Paid from your own pocket. Leave empty to use the risk premiums now deducted from the accounts ({{amount}} per month).
section.monthlyCostKeepHelperUnknown: Paid from your own pocket. Your accounts do not state a risk premium, so enter the amount the fund asks for.
section.monthlyCostTermHelper: The monthly premium from the insurer's quote, in today's money. The premium rises with age and needs medical underwriting.
section.termEndAgeHelper: Leave empty to end it at the age the cover is needed until.
section.keepPaying: Assume I can keep paying personally after the 24-month insurance arrangement
section.keepPayingNote: Whether someone who no longer earns may keep paying into the cover depends on the fund's rules. Ask the fund; switch this off to see the cover end when the arrangement ends.
section.onFileTitle: Cover on file for these accounts
section.onFileNote: From your active pension and savings accounts. It lapses when the deposits stop.
section.onFileRisk: Monthly risk premium inside the deposits
section.onFileSurvivors: Monthly survivors' pension to the spouse
section.onFileNone: No cover details found on the active accounts. Import the Clearing House report, or fill in the insurance coverage fields of each account.
section.derivedNoPlan: No choice saved yet: this shows what happens if you do nothing.
section.derivedGap: Not covered: from age {{from}} to age {{to}} ({{years}} years).
section.derivedNoGap: No gap: the cover reaches the age it is needed until ({{age}}).
section.derivedCost: Cost of the cover: about {{total}} in total ({{monthly}} per month for {{years}} years), paid from your own pocket.
section.derivedCostUnknown: Cost not known yet: enter the monthly cost above to see the total.
section.derivedSurvivors: The accounts insure a survivors' pension of {{insured}} per month. Without the insurance, the balance alone would pay about {{balance}} per month, so the gap in money is about {{gap}} per month.
section.derivedSurvivorsNoFactor: {{accounts}} account(s) show no conversion factor, so the gap is an upper bound.
section.derivedSurvivorsNote: A rough estimate: the balance is projected to the start of the gap and divided by the account's conversion factor. Orphans' pensions and lump sums are not counted.

options.none: Nothing: rely on savings (no extra cost)
options.keepPensionInsurance: Keep the pension insurance going (personal deposits)
options.termLife: Buy an independent term life policy

optionHelp.none: The cover continues for the free extension only, about 5 months after the last deposit.
optionHelp.keepPensionInsurance: An insurance arrangement can extend the cover for up to 24 months at your cost. Beyond that, it depends on the fund letting you keep paying.
optionHelp.termLife: A term policy from the free extension's end to the age you set. You pay the premium; there is probably no tax relief without income.

clearingHouse.title: Import from the Pension Clearing House
clearingHouse.entryTitle: Have a Pension Clearing House report?
clearingHouse.entryBody: Import the consolidated pension report (zip or XML files) from the Pension Clearing House (HaMaslaka HaPensionit, swiftness.co.il) to add all your accounts at once. The files are read on this device only; nothing is uploaded.
clearingHouse.entryHint: Have a Pension Clearing House report? Import it to add all your accounts at once. The files are read on this device only.

entryButtonFor.spouse: Import my partner's Clearing House report

sample.title: Want to see how it works first?
sample.body: Try a sample report for a made-up person. It shows what an import looks like with realistic data. Nothing is added to your plan unless you choose to add it.
sample.bannerBody: This report is for a fictional person and is here only to show how the import works. It is not your data.
sample.apply: Add sample accounts to my plan
sample.confirm: I understand this adds made-up accounts to the plan I already have
sample.confirmHelp: Your plan already has data. The sample accounts would be added next to it and would change your results. The sample never updates your existing accounts.
sample.doneSummary: Made-up accounts added: {{accounts}}. Profile details filled in: {{personal}}.
sample.doneReminder: These accounts are for demonstration only. When you are done, use "Remove sample accounts" in the notice at the top of the page, or clear everything with "Reset all data" in Settings.
sample.dataTitle: Sample accounts are part of your results
sample.dataBody_one: 1 made-up account from the sample report is counted in every figure in the app. These results are not your own.
sample.dataBody_other: {{count}} made-up accounts from the sample report are counted in every figure in the app. These results are not your own.
sample.removeConfirmBody: Only the accounts that came from the sample report are removed. Accounts you added or imported yourself stay. Profile details the sample filled in, such as age or salary, also stay; check them on the Personal step.

clearingHouse.privacy: Your files are read on this device only. Nothing is uploaded and the password is not stored. Of the customer details in the report, only the first name, the age and a one-way fingerprint are kept, to tell reports apart; the ID number, family name and birth date are not.

instructions.title: How to get your report
instructions.step1: Go to swiftness.co.il, the Pension Clearing House (HaMaslaka HaPensionit), and order the consolidated pension report. You verify your identity and pay a small fee.
instructions.step2: The report arrives by email, usually about one business day later, as a password-protected zip file. The email says which password to use.
instructions.step3: Choose that zip file below, or the XML files inside it. If the zip is protected, you will be asked for the password from the email.
instructions.otherFiles: The Excel and PDF files in the package are not needed.

password.title: This file is password protected
password.body: Enter the password from the email that came with the report. It is used only to open the file on this device.
password.label: Zip file password

errors.noXmlFiles: No XML report files were found. Choose the zip file you received, or the XML files from inside it.
errors.tooManyFiles: That is more files than a report normally contains. Choose the zip file, or just the report's XML files.
errors.tooLarge: These files are too large to be a pension report.
errors.passwordRequired: This zip file needs a password.
errors.wrongPassword: That password did not open the file. Check the email and try again.
errors.unreadableArchive: This zip file could not be opened. It may be damaged, or it may not be the file from the Pension Clearing House.
errors.invalidXml: One of the XML files could not be read. Use the files exactly as they came from the Pension Clearing House.
errors.notClearingHouseReport: These files do not look like a Pension Clearing House report.
errors.noAccounts: The report does not contain any pension or savings accounts.
errors.sampleUnavailable: The sample report could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
errors.unknown: Something went wrong while reading the files.

review.title: Review before importing
review.ignored: Other files in the package that were ignored: {{count}}.
review.recognised: This is the same person as the report you imported on {{date}}, so it is saved under the same owner.
review.whoseHelp: A report covers one person. The accounts are saved under the owner you choose.
review.ownerSuggestedSpouse: This is set to your partner because the report fits your partner's details better than yours. Change it if that is wrong.
review.partnerNotCounted: Your partner's accounts will be saved but not counted in your plan until your marital status is Married and your partner's age is entered.

ownerCheck.title: This report may be about someone else
ownerCheck.intro: It does not match what is already in your profile. Saving it under the wrong person would add accounts to them and could overwrite their details. If it belongs to the other person, change the owner above.
ownerCheck.genderDiffers_self: The gender in the report differs from the one in your details.
ownerCheck.genderDiffers_spouse: The gender in the report differs from the one in your partner's details.
ownerCheck.ageDiffers_self: The report is for someone aged {{reportAge}}, but your age is entered as {{profileAge}}.
ownerCheck.ageDiffers_spouse: The report is for someone aged {{reportAge}}, but your partner's age is entered as {{profileAge}}.
ownerCheck.matchesOtherOwner_self: The report matches accounts that are saved under your partner.
ownerCheck.matchesOtherOwner_spouse: The report matches accounts that are saved under you.
ownerCheck.samePersonOtherOwner_self: This looks like the same person as a report you imported under your partner.
ownerCheck.samePersonOtherOwner_spouse: This looks like the same person as a report you imported under you.
ownerCheck.differentPerson_self: This report is about a different person than the report you imported earlier as yours.
ownerCheck.differentPerson_spouse: This report is about a different person than the report you imported earlier as your partner's.
ownerCheck.multiplePeople: The files are about more than one person.
ownerCheck.titleMixed: These files are about different people
ownerCheck.introMixed: Everything is saved under the owner you choose, so one person's accounts would be mixed with another's. It is better to import one person's files at a time.
ownerCheck.confirmMixed_self: I confirm all of these files should be saved as mine
ownerCheck.confirmMixed_spouse: I confirm all of these files should be saved as my partner's
ownerCheck.confirm_self: I confirm this is my report
ownerCheck.confirm_spouse: I confirm this is my partner's report

review.personalHelp: The report also holds a few personal details. Tick the ones to copy to your profile.
review.nothingToImport: Nothing in this report can be imported.
review.matched: This looks like an account you already entered.

projection.title: The provider's projection at age {{age}}, if deposits continue:
projection.note: These are the provider's own assumptions, shown for comparison. The annuity figures above are taken from them where they apply to this account, and you can untick any of them.

review.factorNotGuaranteed: This factor is an estimate, not a guarantee. The app uses it only once you tick "Has guaranteed conversion factor" on the account.
review.nothingSelected: Tick at least one value to import.
review.confirmFirst: Tick the confirmation above to continue.

controls.label: Selection controls
controls.shown: Showing the selected values of {{shown}} of {{total}} accounts.

done.title: Import complete
done.reminder: Open each account to check it and to add what the report does not contain, such as the spouse's details or a salary base for accounts without one.

warnings.policyNumberIsHolderId: The report uses your ID number as the policy number (new pension funds work this way). It is kept in your saved data on this device only, so you can match the account to your statements, and it is left out of the verification pack.
warnings.productTypeUnknown: The product type is not recognised, so the category was left empty. Choose it yourself after importing.
warnings.pensionTypeUnknown: The report does not say which kind of pension fund this is, so the category was left empty.
warnings.pensionTypeBasic: The report calls this a basic pension fund, which the app has no category for. It is suggested as a general pension fund: please confirm.
warnings.oldPensionFund: This is an old ("vatika") pension fund. The app has no separate category for these, so it is suggested as a general pension fund and ticked: untick it if you disagree. Its monthly pension is taken from the fund's own projection.
warnings.statusUnknown: The account status code ({{code}}) is not recognised, so the status was not imported.
warnings.contributionRatesDerived: Contribution rates were calculated from the latest deposits and the salary on the policy.
warnings.contributionRatesMissingSalary: The report has deposits but no salary, so some contribution rates could not be calculated.
warnings.contributionTypeNotModelled: The account has a kind of deposit the app does not model (type {{type}}), so it was left out.
warnings.feeRowsDiffer: The report lists more than one management fee for this account. The highest plausible one is suggested: please check it.
warnings.feesAllZero: The report shows zero fees, which usually means "not reported" rather than free, so fees were not imported.
warnings.feeAccumulationMismatch: The annual fee from accumulation ({{structure}}%) does not match the monthly fee actually charged ({{reported}}% a year). Please check it.
warnings.trackFromDepositOnly: Only the track for new deposits is named in the report, so it is suggested here and ticked: untick it if the existing balance is invested in a different track.
warnings.trackDiffersFromDeposit: New deposits go to a different track than the existing balance. The balance's track is shown.
warnings.negativeBalance: The report shows a negative balance, so the balance was not imported.
warnings.joinDateImplausible: The join date looks implausible, so it was not imported.
warnings.controlCountMismatch: The report says it holds {{declared}} {{what}}, but {{parsed}} were found. Some files may be missing.
warnings.staleReport: This report is {{months}} months old. Balances may be out of date: consider ordering a new one.
warnings.newerSchemaVersion: This report uses a newer format (version {{version}}) than the app was built for. Check the results carefully.
warnings.personalConflict: The files disagree about this detail ({{field}}), so it was not suggested.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.body: Your data stays on this device. Nothing is uploaded to a server, and there is no account.
privacy.short: Your data stays on this device. Nothing is uploaded.

section.title: Privacy
section.stored: Everything you enter is saved in this browser only. There is no account and no server that holds your data.
section.rates: Exchange rates: the app can ask for the dollar rate, sending just the currency pair and a date. You can switch this off below.
section.cpi: Inflation figures: the Assumptions page can ask the Israeli Central Bureau of Statistics for the consumer price index. Nothing about you is sent. You can switch this off below.
section.stocks: Stock prices: choosing a ticker loads that stock's public price file from this site. None of your amounts, dates or other details are sent.
section.files: Files you export or import stay with you. The app never uploads them.

reminder.title: Download a backup of your plan
reminder.bodyNever: Your plan is stored only in this browser, and clearing browser data would erase it. Download a copy and keep it somewhere safe; you can load it back from Settings.
reminder.bodyOverdue: You last exported your plan on {{date}}. Download a fresh copy so your recent changes are safe.
reminder.done: Backup downloaded. Keep the file somewhere safe.

settings.title: Settings

persistence.persisted: Your browser has agreed to keep this plan.
persistence.notPersisted: Your browser may clear this plan if the device runs low on space or you clear browsing data. Export your data to keep a copy.
persistence.unsupported: Your browser cannot confirm that it will keep this plan. Export your data to keep a copy.
persistence.ask: Ask my browser to keep this plan
persistence.safari: Safari, and every browser on an iPhone or iPad, may erase a site's data after about a week without a visit. Export your data regularly, and add this app to your Home Screen if you can.

settings.fxCurrent: Current rate: ₪{{rate}} per US dollar (Bank of Israel, {{date}}). Checked every hour while the app is open.
settings.fxCurrentUnavailable: The current rate could not be loaded. It will be tried again within the hour.
settings.fxLookupPrivacy: When on, the app asks Frankfurter (frankfurter.dev), which publishes the Bank of Israel's rates, for the dollar rate: today's rate to value your holdings, and the rate on each grant or purchase date you enter. Only the currency pair and a date are sent, with no cookies and no referrer. Turn it off to type the rates yourself. None of your other data is ever sent.
settings.cpiLookupPrivacy: When on, the Assumptions page asks the Central Bureau of Statistics (api.cbs.gov.il) for the Israeli consumer price index, to show recent inflation for reference. The request carries nothing about you: no cookies and no referrer. Turn it off to see the table built into the app instead.
settings.resetConfirmBody: This permanently deletes all profile data stored on this device. This cannot be undone.
settings.importError: Couldn't import this file. Please choose a valid exported profile JSON.
settings.importSuccessWithRestore: Data imported. Your previous plan is saved and can be restored from Data management.

importPreview.title: Replace your current plan?
importPreview.intro: Importing {{fileName}} replaces everything in your current plan. The two are not merged.
importPreview.emptiedWarning: The file has nothing for: {{areas}}. Those parts of your plan will be emptied.
importPreview.restoreNote: Your current plan is saved first, so you can undo this from Settings → Data management.

restore.button: Restore the plan from before the last import
restore.hint: Saved {{date}}. Only the latest one is kept.
restore.confirmBody: This replaces your current plan with the one you had before the last import (saved {{date}}). Changes made since the import will be lost.

verification.title: Calculation verification
verification.intro: Export every calculation step behind your results so an independent reviewer (a person or an AI session) can re-check the numbers offline.
verification.ageHelp: Allowed: {{min}}–{{max}}. A spouse in the plan retires the same number of years earlier or later than in the standard scenario.
verification.keyHelp: Maps the aliases in the pack (acct1, holding1…) back to your accounts. Keep it on this device and don't share it.
verification.privacy: Account, holding and vesting ids are replaced by aliases, and provider names, policy numbers, fund ids, tickers and other free text are removed. Redacted is not anonymous: the pack still contains your balances, salary, ages and dates. Share it only with someone you trust with that.
verification.leakError: Export stopped: the pack still contained text from your data. Nothing was saved.
